articles.title: Aditya-L1 reveals new insights into solar eruptions - Nagaland Post
articles.content: Infotainment Aditya-L1 reveals new insights into solar eruptions Aditya-L1 reveals new insights into solar eruptions November 4, 2026 India’s first space-based solar observatory, Aditya-L1, has helped scientists uncover new details about the behaviour of coronal mass ejections (CMEs) beneficial for space-weather studies and thereby affecting satellites and communication networks, an official statement said on Tuesday. The statement from the Ministry of Science & Technology said observations revealed for the first time that these massive solar eruptions do not expand uniformly as previously assumed. These differences in CME expansion can affect its speed as it travels towards Earth causing space-weather disturbances. Researchers from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) combined observations from the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) aboard Aditya-L1 with data from NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and three-dimensional modelling to reconstruct the full 3-D geometry and dynamics of a CME. “The asymmetric shape of an early CME can have important implications for how it interacts with the solar wind and experiences drag during its propagation through the heliosphere. Such effects can influence the CME’s speed and, ultimately, its arrival time at Earth”, said Jayant Joshi of IIA and a co-author of the study published in Astrophysical Journal Letters. Aditya L 1 satellite launched in September 2023 is now operational at the Sun–Earth L1 point, providing continuous observations of the Sun. It carries 7 payloads, of which the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), the primary payload, is an internally occulted coronagraph designed to observe the solar corona simultaneously in various modes. The model was used to test how the CME’s orientation and uneven sideways expansion could produce the spectral structures observed by VELC. (IANS) The researchers plan to use this technique on other CMEs, to reconstruct their motion without relying entirely on multi-viewpoint imaging from telescopes in space. This complementarity is particularly valuable in the lower corona, where CMEs evolve rapidly, and their motion along the line of sight cannot be obtained from imaging alone, the statement noted. articles.title: Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu Wins India's First Youth Olympic Wushu Medal - GKToday
articles.content: Home Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu Wins India's First Youth Olympic Wushu Medal Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu Wins India's First Youth Olympic Wushu Medal November 4, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 On 3 November 2026, 15-year-old Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu of Manipur won bronze in the women's Changquan combined event at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, securing India's first-ever wushu medal at the event. Changquan Combined Event Chanu scored 18.039 points, comprising 8.723 in Gunshu and 9.316 in Changquan. Egypt's Sondos Sonbol won gold with 18.660 points, while Venezuela's Valeria Frannerys Dudamel Alvarado took silver with 18.199. Wushu made its debut as a medal sport at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games , which are being held in Dakar—the first time the event has taken place in Africa. India's Medal Tally Chanu's bronze was India's third medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics, alongside Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada's silver in judo and Dhinidhi Desinghu's bronze in swimming. Chanu had previously won bronze in the girls' youth Changquan event at the 2026 World Junior Wushu Championships in Tianjin, China. Important Facts for Exams Wushu competition disciplines: Competitive wushu has two principal disciplines: taolu, judged routines using empty-hand or weapons forms, and sanda, a full-contact combat sport. Gunshu judging distinction: Gunshu is a taolu routine using the staff; unlike sanda bouts, its result comes from judges’ technical and performance scores rather than points scored against an opponent. YOG mixed-NOC format: Youth Olympic Games have included selected mixed-NOC events, pairing athletes from different National Olympic Committees in the same competition. Karnataka Plans India’s 1st Mobile Biodiversity Museum Inside Volvo Bus Volvo is also donating a 15-metre 9600 Series model multi-axle luxury coach for this one-of-a-kind mobile museum in Karnataka. by Ashmeet Guliani Updated: November 04, 2026 12:22 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Canva Pro/ Apriori1 and Instants (Representative Image) Karnataka is planning something big! “Western Ghats on Wheels” is an exciting new project in the state. It is India’s first mobile biodiversity museum, which aims to bring the magic of the Western Ghats rainforests directly to students and tourists without them having to travel to a forest. Here’s what we know so far. Karnataka To Launch “Western Ghats On Wheels?” Museums are a perfect way to learn about history, nature or, in general, any topic in the world. And now, the Karnataka government is all set to launch India’s first mobile biodiversity museum. According to The New Indian Express, “ Western Ghats on Wheels” will be set up inside a Volvo bus. It will travel across the state, including rural areas, and cater to different sections of society. The bus has been approved for the mobile museum, and the project will launch in the next six months. Planned at a cost of ₹1 crore, the project is truly unique. Reportedly, Volvo is also donating a 15-metre 9600 Series model multi-axle luxury coach for this one-of-a-kind mobile museum. Also Read: Bengaluru To Goa In 13 Hours: New Vande Bharat Via Western Ghats Likely In November What Will Tourists Get To See Inside This Moving Museum? Now, let’s talk about what tourists will get to witness inside the bus. According to The New Indian Express, interactive and holographic screens will be installed inside to showcase the wildlife, waterfalls and forests of the Western Ghats. In addition, the bus will operate using roof-mounted solar panels to ensure a zero-carbon footprint. Inside, there will be three sections. The two sides will be used as corridors, occupying three-fourths of the bus, with interactive displays. The remaining space will be used for seating and discussions. Officials are also planning to display theme-based, life-sized models inside. Images and videos used to create virtual experiences of the Western Ghats will be sourced from different places. To ensure that children remain attentive, there will also be graphic and animation-based displays. Also Read: Karnataka’s Famous Sweet, Belagavi Kunda, Is Now An Ice Cream! Where You Can Get It? articles.title: Purba Bardhaman Innovator Wins International Award for Blood-Clotting Technology
articles.content: Home Purba Bardhaman Innovator Wins International Award for Blood-Clotting Technology Purba Bardhaman Innovator Wins International Award for Blood-Clotting Technology November 4, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 On 4 November 2026, Sabir Hossain, an innovator from Badulia village in the Khandaghosh block of Purba Bardhaman district, West Bengal, received the top prize in the Health and Biomedical category at Slingshot 2026 in Singapore. Blood-clotting technology Hossain’s startup, Miracules Medsolutions, developed StopBleed, a powder designed to control severe bleeding within 60 seconds. The product uses nano-biopolymers that rapidly absorb blood plasma and trap blood cells, accelerating the body’s natural clotting process. It has been approved by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). Slingshot 2026 attracted more than 5,000 startups worldwide. Along with the award, Miracules Medsolutions received a grant of 400,000 Singapore dollars. Important Facts for Exams Cellular and protein components: Coagulation combines cellular components, including platelets, with protein-based clotting factors. Primary and secondary haemostasis: Platelets first form a temporary plug; clotting factors then generate fibrin strands that strengthen it. Fibrin stabilisation: Near the end of the clotting cascade, factor XIIIa cross-links fibrin, stabilising the clot as it temporarily seals the wound. The policy targets river health and flood control, and it also finds a use for the removed silt. Here are some of the key facts about Bihar’s New Silt Management Policy 2026: Its official name is the Bihar Water Source Restoration and Silt Management Policy, 2026 . Silt is a fine, soil-like material that rivers carry along and drop once the current slows. Silt management means measuring how much has piled up, removing it, transporting it and finding a safe use for it. The policy treats all of this as one connected process. Here are some major objectives of Bihar’s Silt Management Policy 2026 Bihar has teamed up with NHAI, which works under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH). Desilting will begin only after technical checks, with environmental safeguards in place. The Nadi Sanjeevani initiative aims at cleaning rivers and building highways . Usable silt taken out of rivers will serve as filling material for national highway works, so one task helps both. Bihar sits in the Ganga basin, and many rivers from the Himalayas in Nepal flow through it. In the monsoon they bring huge amounts of sediment. When this settles, riverbeds become shallow and water has less room to flow. The result is: Policy help in flood control - Removing silt from the most affected spots lets rivers carry water more freely. This can reduce waterlogging and ease pressure at selected locations during the monsoon. Improve water supply - Desilting brings back the storage capacity of rivers, canals and reservoirs. This helps keep water available for irrigation and daily use....

articles.title: Gold itna paas tha kaise jaane deti, says India's first woman wrestling world champion ...
articles.content: Gold itna paas tha kaise jaane deti, says India’s first woman wrestling world champion Manisha Bhanwala Manisha Bhanwala has become India’s first woman wrestling world champion winning gold in the 59kg freestyle category at the World Championships in Astana. Published on: Nov 4, 2026, 11:28:08 IST By Karan Sethi Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link Making history called for a special celebration, and wrestler Manisha Bhanwala knew just what to do. After becoming India’s first woman wrestling world champion in the 59kg freestyle category at the World Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, last week, the 29-year-old from Haryana broke into football star Cristiano Ronaldo’s iconic ‘Siuuu’ celebration. Manisha Bhanwala celebrates after her gold win. “I got up from the mat and it suddenly hit me that I am a World Champion, that too India’s first. Toh bas mujhe kuch dhaakad si celebration karni thi,” she tells us, adding, “No one really expected me or a wrestler to do the Siuuu celebration and I think that’s why it became such a fun moment.” The victory, however, was far from easy. Trailing 1-6 at the break in the final, Manisha drew on the mental strength she says she has learnt from watching top athletes across sports. “Final mein jab main down thi, tab kahin na kahin mere mind ne mujhe bola ki abhi nahi rukna and tu hi jeetegi kyunki tune aise hi din ke liye din raat mehnat kari hai. Gold mere itna paas tha, aise kaise jaane de deti.” Back home in her village in Rohtak, Manisha is being celebrated by family, friends and neighbours. But amid the festivities, she misses her father, Suresh Bhanwala, who died in 2022. She had worn a T-shirt in his memory before the bout. She says, “My father was and will always be my angel, my rock.” Htcity Wrestler Gold Medal Home / Htcity / Htcity Delhi Junction / Gold Itna Paas Tha Kaise Jaane Deti, Says India’s First Woman Wrestling World Champion Manisha Bhanwala See Less Home / Htcity / Htcity Delhi Junction / Gold Itna Paas Tha Kaise Jaane Deti, Says India’s First Woman Wrestling World Champion Manisha Bhanwala

articles.title: Aditya-L1 reveals uneven solar eruptions, could improve space weather predictions
articles.content: CHENNAI: Providing new insights on solar eruptions, India's first dedicated solar observation spacecraft, Aditya-L1, has revealed that they do not always expand uniformly. The findings could help scientists improve space weather predictions and assess the potential impact of solar activity on satellite s. These powerful eruptions from the Sun affects several technologies people depend on every day, including GPS navigation, satellite communication, electricity networks, and mobile services. Using observations from Aditya-L1, ISRO scientists recently discovered that solar eruptions do not always expand uniformly. According to the findings, observations from the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) aboard the vessel have revealed that a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME, ) a massive release of charged particles and magnetic fields from the Sun, expanded asymmetrically in the region close to the solar surface. Their analysis combining imaging observations, spectroscopic measurements from VELC, and three-dimensional modelling found that conventional models, which assumed CMEs expanded symmetrically like bubbles, could not reproduce the spectral patterns recorded by the instrument. However, when scientists introduced asymmetric lateral expansion and a tilted structure into their three-dimensional model, the simulated spectra closely matched the actual VELC observations. This provided evidence that the CME had expanded unevenly in the inner corona, challenging the earlier assumption that such eruptions always maintain a uniform structure. The discovery is significant, because the shape of a CME can influence how it travels through space. Depending on its structure, a solar eruption may experience different levels of resistance from the solar wind, affecting its speed and the time it takes to reach Earth. When powerful CMEs interact with Earth's magnetic field, they can trigger geomagnetic storms that have the potential to disrupt satellite operations, GPS navigation, radio communications and, in severe cases, electricity transmission networks. The study demonstrates how Aditya-L1's VELC instrument can help scientists determine the three-dimensional structure of solar eruptions from a single observation point. These findings could help scientists better assess potential threats to Earth's technology-dependent infrastructure and support the design and development of satellites with improved protection against the effects of solar storms. Launched on September 2, 2023, aboard the PSLV-C57 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Aditya-L1 is India's first space-based solar observatory. The spacecraft was placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), approximately 1.5 million km from Earth. Its primary objective is to study the Sun's outer layers.

articles.title: Rajkumari wins India's first wushu medal at Youth Olympics - Hindustan Times
articles.content: Rajkumari wins India's first wushu medal at Youth Olympics She won bronze in women’s changquan combined wushu event Published on: Nov 3, 2026, 23:56:32 IST By HT Correspondent Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu won a historic bronze medal for India in wushu at the Youth Olympic Games 2026 in Dakar, Senegal on Tuesday, taking the country's medal tally to three. Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu Rajkumari won bronze in the women’s changquan combined wushu event. She scored 8.723 in gunshu and 9.316 in changquan for a combined total of 18.039, finishing third. Egypt’s Sondos Sonbol claimed the gold medal with a total score of 18.660 while Venezuela’s Valeria Frannerys Dudamel Alvarado took silver (18.199). This is the first time that wushu is part of Youth Olympics programme as a medal sport. The changquan combined event is a routine-based (taolu) wushu discipline that combines a bare-handed routine and a weapon routine. The scores of both are added for a final total. The competition spanned three days and the top eight qualified for the final round. Rajkumari placed second among 12 athletes in the preliminary stage with a total of 17.982. Rajkumari, who hails from Manipur, was the only Indian in wushu and displayed remarkable grit to win a medal. This was India's third medal at the Dakar Youth Olympics. On Monday, Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada won silver in the women’s judo (63kg category) and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu bagged bronze in the women’s 100m freestyle. "Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu has created history for Indian wushu by winning first-ever medal in the sport at the Youth Olympics. It was possible because of her hard work and determination and the hard work of coached and support staff," the Wushu Association of India said in a statement.
